decisive_items: 2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene
lens dislocation superonasally in the right eye
hypermobility of shoulders, digits, and knees
response.rationale: LTBP2 mutations are known to cause Weill-Marchesani syndrome, which fits the lens dislocation, elevated IOP, and joint hypermobility. Marfan syndrome is less likely due to normal echocardiograms and absence of FBN1 mutation.

rejected.why: Pseudoexfoliation syndrome is atypical for this age and lacks characteristic anterior segment findings; open angle and no pseudoexfoliation material.
Ehlers-Danlos syndrome typically features skin hyperextensibility and does not explain lens dislocation or LTBP2 variants.
Marfan syndrome is suggested by tall stature and lens dislocation, but normal echocardiograms, negative family history, and LTBP2 (not FBN1) variants argue against it.
